title: Android Fundamentals
objectives: Explain the role of the manifest and the build system
Understand the APK/AAB and the Android runtime

sections.markdown: An Android app is a set of components (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, ContentProviders) declared in a manifest, compiled to an APK/AAB, and run on the ART runtime atop a customized Linux kernel.

rows: A single screen / UI entry point

sections.markdown:
## The manifest
AndroidManifest.xml declares components, permissions, the min/target SDK, and the launcher activity. The system reads it to know what your app contains before running any code.
Apps run on **ART** (Android Runtime), which uses AOT + JIT compilation. Each app runs in its own process and sandbox (a unique Linux user ID) for isolation and security.
Ship an **AAB** (Android App Bundle), not a raw APK — Play generates optimized per-device APKs, shrinking download size.
